key_insight: ALER-TI improves time series imputation by retrieving useful latent patterns from aligned embeddings, instead of depending only on nearby corrupted observations. This helps reconstruct missing values when local context is weak, noisy, or non-stationary.
problem_solved: The paper addresses the difficulty of imputing missing values in time series with weak temporal correlations, irregular patterns, and non-stationary behavior, where standard local-context-based deep models often fail.
method: Learn latent embeddings that capture richer time series representations beyond the raw observed neighborhood.
Retrieve aligned latent information from similar patterns to support reconstruction of missing segments.
Use the retrieved embedding context to guide imputation when local temporal clues are insufficient.
impact: For AI/ML practitioners, this offers a more robust imputation strategy for messy real-world time series such as sensor streams, healthcare signals, and industrial data. It can improve downstream forecasting, anomaly detection, and decision-making by producing more reliable completed sequences.
visual_elements: Pipeline diagram showing corrupted time series -> latent embedding -> retrieval -> imputed output
Side-by-side comparison of baseline local imputation vs ALER-TI reconstruction
Heatmap or embedding space visualization showing aligned latent retrieval
Timeline graphic highlighting missing points and recovered values
paper_title: ALER-TI: Aligned Latent Embedding Retrieval for Time Series Imputation
paper_authors: Xuan-Thong Truong, Trung-Kien Le, Tung Kieu, Thi-Thu Nguyen, Nhat-Hai Nguyen
